transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Time: 11:00 AM PT
Duration: 38 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Miguel Santos (Harbor - Head of ML Ops), Aisha Khan (Harbor - Dir Platform), Tom Lee (Harbor - Procurement)
Links shared: security pack (https://redwood.example/sec-pack.pdf), pricing spreadsheet (link sent after call)

Summary:
Quick renewal check-in; Harbor interested in adding two additional regions (eu-west and ap-southeast), upgrading Dedicated capacity for peak holiday throughput, and discussing 12-month contract extension with discounted committed capacity. Customer asked for private deployment options for some regulated data and a benchmark run to validate p95 latency under multi-tenant load.

Topics:
- Capacity sizing and burst policy
- Additional regions and data residency
- Contract length, pricing and discounts
- Private deployment / VPC networking and KMS
- Benchmarks and next steps

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Kim: Hey everyone thanks for joining, how's it goin' from your side?
[00:04] Miguel Santos: Good, thanks Jordan. Busy week but, uh, good to catch up. We have Aisha and Tom on as well.
[00:08] Aisha Khan: Hi all.
[00:09] Tom Lee: Hello.
[00:11] Jordan Kim: Quick agenda — renewal numbers, capacity ask, regions, and then tech follow-up (Priya will cover benchmarks). Sound ok?
[00:16] Miguel Santos: Yep that's perfect. We just want to make sure we can handle holiday spikes and expansion into EU and APAC next quarter.
[00:24] Priya Nair: Great, I can cover the options: dedicated pools vs hosted with reserved capacity, plus burst. We also have private deployment options for regulated pipelines.
[00:31] Miguel Santos: So our main asks — one, bump Dedicated baseline from 8 GPUs to 16 for Q4 spikes; two, add eu-west and ap-southeast as active regions; three, keep data for payment tokens in our private deployment only.
[00:45] Jordan Kim: Understood. On the 16 GPU baseline — we can structure as committed capacity with monthly overage or a baseline plus burst credits. Burst credits let you absorb short spikes without long-term cost.
[00:58] Aisha Khan: Cost is important — what does the unit economics look like if we go 12 months vs 24 months on committed?
[01:06] Jordan Kim: Typically we can offer a 10-15% discount on a 12-month commit, and 18-25% on 24-month depending on total committed tokens/GPU hours. I'll send a pricing table after the call.
[01:18] Tom Lee: If we extend to 24 months we need an escape for material breach and SLAs, can your legal team include that?
[01:24] Jordan Kim: Yes, our legal can include standard termination for convenience and SLA credits. We'll pull in pricing + draft amendment.
[01:30] Priya Nair: For regions — we can provision dedicated pools in eu-west and ap-southeast. Note that provisioning lead time is about 4-6 weeks for dedicated in a new region unless you want hosted capacity there initially. Also, routing and cross-region failover is configurable.
[01:43] Miguel Santos: 4-6 weeks is fine. One nuance — in EU we need logs retained for 7 years for one partner, and a local data residency requirement. Can Redwood support per-region retention and audit log separation?
[01:57] Priya Nair: Yes, we have per-route retention policies and can configure audit log exports to a region-specific S3 bucket or customer-managed logging. For private deployments, you can keep audit logs entirely on-prem.
[02:08] Aisha Khan: KMS — we need to ensure customer-managed keys for production keys.
[02:12] Jordan Kim: We support KMS/HSM integrations; we'll include the integration guide in the security pack.
[02:16] Tom Lee: On the private deployment piece, what parts remain in Redwood control plane vs customer-managed? We have a tight network posture.
[02:23] Priya Nair: For Private, control plane can be customer-managed in a VPC. The runtime components sit in your network; we provide a lightweight ops agent and the control plane API. Network diagrams will show required egress and peering — we'll send those.
[02:35] Miguel Santos: Perfect. For the benchmark, we want Priya's team to run a 24-hour stress test simulating our traffic profile, focusing on p95 latency and tail latencies during cache misses.
[02:46] Priya Nair: We'll need your sample prompt corpus and typical sequence length distribution. Also, what p95 target are you trying to hold?
[02:54] Miguel Santos: Ideally p95 under 400ms for generation requests when cached; p99 under 1.2s. During holiday peaks we'd accept slightly higher p95 if throughput is maintained.
[03:05] Priya Nair: Ok that maps to using a mix of batching + KV prefix caching and a 16-GPU dedicated pool with auto-burst. We'll propose batching settings and a test harness to reproduce tail behaviour.
[03:16] Aisha Khan: On compliance docs — can you share SOC 2 docs and the ISO cert?
[03:20] Jordan Kim: Yes, included in the security pack link; also we'll share the SOC2 report under NDA if needed.
[03:26] Tom Lee: Procurement — timeline likely end of March. We need updated pricing and a simple amendment so our legal can review before PO.
[03:33] Jordan Kim: We'll aim to send pricing and amendment by Friday 3/6.
[03:36] Miguel Santos: Quick question — we've been running against your hosted endpoint for two years and seen a cost uptick. We're trying to compare Redwood Dedicated vs Vertex/Anthropic managed for cost. Any notes?
[03:46] Priya Nair: Dedicated tends to reduce per-token unit cost if you have sustained throughput because GPU utilization is higher and you can tune quantization and batching. We'll include a cost modeling spreadsheet comparing dedicated vs hosted vs cloud vendors.
[03:57] Miguel Santos: Great. Also, can Redwood support regional cold-starts — we want a warm KV cache policy when we spin up new instances to avoid initial tail latency.
[04:06] Priya Nair: Yes — you can preload prefix caches and snapshot KV cache across instances. For private, that's in your control; for hosted/dedicated we can orchestrate warm-up using our rollout hooks.
[04:17] Aisha Khan: Any blockers on the timeline?
[04:19] Jordan Kim: Not from our side — main dependencies are signed amendment, infra details from Aisha, and benchmark data from Miguel.
[04:25] Tom Lee: One more procurement note — our finance group requires invoice net-45 for new vendors. Is that possible?
[04:30] Jordan Kim: Standard is net-30, but we can escalate to finance. I'll flag it in the pricing email.
[04:34] Miguel Santos: Ok, let's recap next steps.
[04:36] Jordan Kim: Sure. Jordan to send pricing and draft amendment (3/6). Priya will send benchmark plan and test harness requirements (3/12). Aisha to upload infra diagram and compliance Qs (3/8). Tom to confirm procurement timeline and PO flow (3/10).
[04:50] Aisha Khan: Sounds good. I'll include the VPC peering contacts.
[04:53] Miguel Santos: Thanks everyone. We'll look out for the security pack NDA for SOC 2.
[04:57] Jordan Kim: I'll attach the SOC2 under NDA and the network diagram. Anything else?
[05:01] Tom Lee: Nothing else from procurement.
[05:03] Priya Nair: I'll follow up with a short doc on benchmark parameters and the sample client to run.
[05:07] Jordan Kim: Thanks all, we'll follow up in email. Bye.
[05:09] Miguel Santos: Bye.

Notes on transcription: occasional word errors (e.g., KV cache heard as KV cash), speaker labels sometimes generic in the recording; content verified by AE post-call.

End of transcript.
